analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING: 1) Jan Hatzius Latest Views, 2) BRL EoD Views, 3) Brazil Webcast Key Quotes, 4) RBNZ & AUD CPI Previews and 5) Earnings This Week
key_insights: Hatzius: 2026 global growth has been 'remarkably unremarkable', with the world and G3 tracking potential as fiscal easing and the AI boom offset drags from the Iran war and US tariffs. The standing 2027 forecast is more of the same, with lower energy prices offsetting fading fiscal and AI tailwinds, but risks are skewed to the downside.
Energy is the most immediate growth concern. Gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and European/Asian gas prices are back near March/April highs on Middle East escalation fears.
DM yield curves are up about 100bp since early 2026. If sustained, higher long-end yields could subtract a cumulative 0.6% from GDP via housing, durables and capex.

The AI growth impulse is set to peak in late 2026/early 2027. AI's ~0.4pp boost to US consumer spending via wealth effects fades gradually in the base case, and more sharply if AI stocks keep declining.

Fed: GS expects a hold on 28 October and a 25bp hike to 4-4.25% on 9 December, because spot inflation is too high and energy adds upside inflation risk. Another hike in March is possible, with renewed cuts in late 2027/early 2028.
ECB: likely holds on 29 October and hikes a final time to 2.75% in December. French bond-market turbulence, likely to cut 1/4-1/2pp from annualised growth, is a downside risk to that call.
BoE: GS expects a 25bp hike to 4% on 5 November, with risk of further moves, though 4+ priced hikes look excessive. Hikes are also expected in Canada and New Zealand this week, and in Australia.
GS's strongest global view is that central banks will deliver fewer hikes than priced.

Cross-asset: rates strategists cite underweight positioning, diminished technical risks and risk asset pressures as reasons the recent rally might extend. Equity strategists are wary of momentum factor exposure given narrow breadth, but expect the S&P 500 to resume its climb after the midterm election.

Credit strategists remain cautious on IG technology bonds but see scope for a near-term reversal in HY after the recent selloff. FX strategists expect the yen to hedge further AI jitters, partly because such jitters would shrink US-Japan rate differentials.
Commodity strategists recommend targeted exposure to oil products and European natural gas as hedges against near-term escalation, plus longer-term exposure to copper, gold and select power markets.

BRL flows: volume was about $80bn yesterday against a $30-40bn average. Flows were balanced, with CTAs buying USD and local corporates selling. The desk is watching how CTAs react to the spike in vol and spot, which can interact badly given December seasonality.

BRL trading view: the desk is running light risk while waiting for the Finance Minister appointment and fiscal measures. Positive headlines include Alckmin as a likely Finance Minister and Camilo Santana as a possible Chief of Staff.

Reports from CNN say Lula's team is considering cutting tax incentives, streamlining social benefits and changing how the constitutional health and education spending floors are calculated, and reaching out to orthodox economists.

Brazil rates: DIs needed a third circuit breaker before trading again yesterday. They trimmed losses after the BRL reversal and the Treasury (NT) announcing a buyback auction, with about 2.5m DV01 announced and about 1.5m placed.

Ramos (LatAm economics): the market wants strong fiscal signals. The campaign's expensive promises have visibly deteriorated the fiscal baseline, and primary spending rose close to 6% YoY in real terms over the last 4 years. Many expect the administration to seek another constitutional amendment before the new term starts, as it did four years ago (>160bn BRL of added primary spending).
Loureiro (LatAm equities trading): Brazilian equities have historically not performed under Lula governments and are just a trading market, not a long-term long.

Marinheiro (Brazil macro trading): first hedge and adjust the portfolio, then wait for levels. FX may trade better than rates long-term because rates should trade higher under restrictive monetary policy, and the FX carry trade could let BRL outperform rates for the next few years.

RBNZ: GS now expects 25bp hikes at both the October and December meetings, to a terminal rate of 3.25% (prior: one 25bp hike in December to 3.00%). It then holds at 3.25%, as spare capacity limits pass-through of higher oil prices and a weaker currency.

AUD CPI preview: GS expects headline CPI of +0.79% m/m, lifting y/y 35bp to 4.32%. Drivers are fuel (+9.0% m/m), domestic travel (+4.1%), international travel (+5.6%) and property rates (+5.0%). Trimmed mean is forecast at +0.29% m/m, leaving y/y little changed at 3.60%.

Earnings week: markets are jittery after Meta raised the low end of its 2026 capex guide, turned FCF-negative and flagged multi-year equity funding needs via new Class C shares. Its CDS spreads widened, and the market is looking for 'growth without another spending shock'.

Hyperscaler results (MSFT and GOOGL Wednesday, AMZN Thursday) are the key test of the AI spending cycle. Further equity issuance or balance-sheet pressure is unlikely to be well received, and cloud growth quality is in focus.
MSFT: stock is up 38% since the July print. GIR sees upside to 46-47% cc Azure growth versus Street 45% (guide 44-45%), and there is a debate on FY28 capex (GSe $319bn vs Street $252bn).
GOOGL: debate is Search resilience versus agentic AI disruption (GIR -1% vs consensus on Q3 Search), offset by Google Cloud (GIR ~+100% y/y vs consensus +96%). GIR capex is $350bn in 2027.
AMZN: focus on AWS growth and margins (consensus ~41%/37%), reports of idle NVDA racks that cannot be switched on for lack of power, and scrutiny of capex upward revisions (~$220bn for 2026).

ORCL Investor Day on the 28th: 10GW capacity roadmap execution, capex intensity and timing (has said 27-28 peak), customer concentration and upside to FY26-30 targets. Samsung and Hynix also report in Asia.

tension_points.bull_case: Positive headlines on likely orthodox Finance Minister names (Alckmin), possible cuts to tax incentives, streamlined social benefits and outreach to orthodox economists. The administration has an incentive to look more orthodox, and the FX carry trade could let BRL outperform rates.
tension_points.bear_case: The fiscal baseline has visibly deteriorated after expensive campaign promises. Primary spending rose close to 6% real YoY over 4 years, equities have historically not performed under Lula, and CTA flows could react badly to the vol spike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Absence of strong fiscal signals, such as a constitutional amendment or measures before the new term starts, would undermine the orthodox-pivot case.

tension_points.bull_case: GIR sees Azure growth upside (46-47% cc vs Street 45%) and Google Cloud growth of ~+100% y/y versus consensus +96%.
tension_points.bear_case: Meta turned FCF-negative and flagged equity funding, with CDS spreads wider. Capex is rising (MSFT FY28 GSe $319bn vs Street $252bn), and Search resilience and idle AWS capacity are open questions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further equity issuance or balance-sheet pressure at the hyperscalers would not be well received.
